descriptionChirho: To place or set an object, person, or abstract entity in a location or position (Qal active, core spatial/positional sense; Arabic وَضَعَ/أَضَعُ, Korean 놓다/두다, Swahili -weka).
To be placed or laid, the passive voice of the core spatial sense (Qal passive; Arabic يوضَعُ/يُوقَفُ, Korean 놓이다, Swahili -wekwa).
To make or render someone or something into a state or role, a causative-transformative extension of 'set' (Qal with جَعَلَ sense; Arabic جَعَلَ/يَجْعَلُ/أُصَيِّرَ, Korean 만들다/세우다, Swahili -fanya).
To appoint or establish someone in an official capacity or fixed arrangement (Qal with specialized designation sense; Arabic عَيَّنَ/أَقَامُوا, Korean 정하다, Swahili -pangia).
To turn or direct one's face or attention toward a target (Qal with directional orientation sense; Arabic وَجَّهَ, Swahili -geuza).
To put on or don clothing or adornment (Qal with vestimentary sense; Swahili vaa 'wear', distinct from general placement).
